name: Khanty
notes: Northern Khanty, Kazym dialect (standard literary Khanty), Ob-Ugric branch, Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: modern Kazym Khanty Cyrillic orthography, NFC (⟨Ӓӓ Ӧӧ Ӱӱ Ӈӈ⟩ are precomposed characters; ⟨ӆ⟩ is the lateral fricative letter, distinct from plain ⟨л⟩). Orthography and phoneme values follow Nikolaeva (1999): ⟨в⟩ is the labio-velar approximant /w/, not Russian /v/; ⟨г⟩ is the fricative /ɣ/; ⟨х⟩ is the uvular fricative /χ/; ⟨ч⟩ is the palatal stop /c/ (not an affricate); ⟨ы⟩ is /ɪ/; ⟨э⟩ is /ə/. The coronals ⟨л⟩ and ⟨н⟩ palatalise to /ʎ/ and /ɲ/ before the iotated vowels ⟨е ё и ю я⟩ and the soft sign ⟨ь⟩ (Nikolaeva 1999, Sec. 2; directly evidenced by NorthEuraLex нёӆ -> ɲ o ɬ, i.e. ⟨нё⟩ realises the single palatal nasal + vowel, not н+jo), so those sequences are entered as multigraph keys the maximal-munch matcher prefers over the bare consonant. Word stress in Khanty is not phonemically distinctive and its placement is disputed among descriptions (Nikolaeva 1999, Sec. 1.3); documented here as an ENGINE-LIMIT stress exemption and not modelled. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): corrected ⟨ӆ⟩ from a retroflex-lateral reading to the lateral FRICATIVE /ɬ/ (NorthEuraLex паӆ -> p a ɬ, ӆыӆ -> ɬɪɬ), ⟨х⟩ from /x/ to the uvular /χ/ (NorthEuraLex тахты -> taχtɪ), ⟨ы⟩ from /ɯ/ to /ɪ/, ⟨э⟩ from /e̞/ to /ə/ (эӆ -> əɬ), and ⟨т⟩ from aspirated /tʰ/ to plain /t/ (NorthEuraLex тут -> tut shows no aspiration marked). Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog. BENCHMARK CAVEAT: the iteration fixes above were diagnosed against NorthEuraLex examples and the spec is scored on that same corpus, so the recorded PER partly reflects same-corpus tuning; each fix is independently cited to Nikolaeva 1999, but treat the number as favorable until a second gold source exists.
